posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
Jim, if I had it to do over again I would invest in some magnetic mounts. They would provide the holding power of my 5 to 10 lb bases with a much smaller profile. As you remember, squeezing in the spatial filter was difficult due to the size of the base of the object transfer mirror and the size of the base of the spatial filter. 

I believe it was Colin that found a very nice source of magnetic mounts that only needed a very small modification for mounting a 1/2 rod to them. I may invest in some. If you want a few let me know and we can order together and may be able to get shipping costs down or get a price break on quantity. If you don’t have a steel top then let me know also and maybe I can sell or give you my existing bases if I decide to get the magnetic ones. I will miss those bases though as I have had them for over 20 years. They have been used on steel, concrete and sand tables but I know they would be going to a good home. A cheap source on Gimbal mounts is next.

Here is the thread in the old forum. Again, I don't believe the posts are 1/2 inch diameter.

posts.author: JohnFlux
posts.content_md:
I personally cannot stand magnetic stands. I'm very clumsy and tend to knock things, and hate when I knock a stand by a millimeter. Also I find it hard to move them accurately - they take a fair amount of force to move.

I used to like the bases you can screw down, but found it hard to move them by a small amount in the direction I want - the nearest hole always been too far away or too close.

My favorite by a long stretch is the design that looks a bit like this:

 r--o--C

one end pushes into to table anywhere (illustrated with the 'r') and one end is a C shape that holds on to the base. Then a bolt goes through the "o". Allows me to hold down posts securely, and yet i can move them with ease.

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
> **JohnFlux:** I personally cannot stand magnetic stands. I'm very clumsy and tend to knock things, and hate when I knock a stand by a millimeter. Also I find it hard to move them accurately - they take a fair amount of force to move.

I've found the Harbor Freight magnetic mounts to be reliable in both areas. I'm often running into a mount in the dark and have only had them move when they aren't turned on. Turn it off and it's as easy to move as any gravity mount. Turn it on and it's locked in place.

BTW, **never** shift a mount around on the table when it's on. Any burr or piece of grit between the mount and the table will cause a deep scratch that can negatively affect the flatness of the table in that area.

posts.author: JohnFlux
posts.content_md: Ah, I didn't realise you were talking about the electromagnetic ones. Those are cool, although I haven't gotten to use them much so can't comment

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md: They aren't electromagnetic. That would be cool though. They just have a rotating magnet inside the base. You don't literally turn them on and off, you just rotate the magnet so that facing the "wrong way" when turned "off".
